sections.title: Gifts given and received, person by person
body: Record what you gave and what you received with the date, the occasion, whose event it was, the amount and how it was given. You can also note a gift item, whether you attended and stayed for the meal, tags, a memo and a thank-you mark. Each person's totals given and received add up, and Your turn and search bring back the records you need.

sections.title: Reminders for upcoming events and birthdays
body: Note a future occasion with its title, type, date, place and memo, and it appears under Upcoming. Each person can have a birthday, including lunar and leap-month birthdays. Turn on reminders in Settings to get one the day before and one on the day of each occasion and birthday.

sections.title: Kept with iCloud and backup files
body: When you are signed in to iCloud, records stay in step across devices on the same Apple Account. In Settings you can make and send a backup file, and merging from a backup file adds only the records you don't have, without overwriting the ones you do. Once a day the app also keeps an automatic copy on this iPhone and holds the latest 14.

sections.title: Start without an account
body: There is no sign-up or login. Turn on the lock in Settings, and the app asks for Face ID or your device passcode when it opens.

pro.title:
No ads,
plus a guestbook, export, statistics and fill-in
items: Fill in from invitation and obituary links or photos

a: Devices signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account keep their records in step through iCloud.

Without iCloud, make a backup file in Settings, send it to the new device, and merge from that backup file on the new device. Merging adds only the records that are missing and does not overwrite the ones you have.

faq.q: Bringing back records from an automatic copy
a: Once a day the app keeps a copy of your records on this iPhone and holds the latest 14. Tap a date under the automatic copies in Settings to add back the records from that day that you no longer have.

Reminders are off at first. When you turn them on in Settings, iOS asks whether to allow notifications. If you allow them, a reminder arrives the day before and on the day of each upcoming occasion and birthday.
If you didn't allow notifications, turn them on in iOS Settings > Notifications > Life Tally.
When the lock is on in Settings, the app opens with Face ID or your device passcode. iOS checks your face, and the app does not receive face data.
If you turn off the device passcode in iPhone Settings after turning on the lock, the app turns the lock off and opens.

faq.q: Filling in from invitations and obituaries
a: With Life Tally Pro, paste a mobile wedding invitation or obituary link or its text, or pick one photo, and the name, date, place and bank account are filled in.
A link is opened in a hidden web view inside the app to read its text, and a photo is read on the iPhone. The app does not send the text or photo it reads anywhere else.

One Google AdMob banner ad appears at the bottom of the Home, People and Settings tabs. There are no ads on the screens and sheets where you write a record, on the lock screen, or in the guestbook for your own events.
With Life Tally Pro, ads disappear, and the app does not ask for personalized ad consent or tracking permission. From the next time you open the app, it does not start the ad SDK either.
When the app gets ads ready, iOS asks whether Life Tally may track you. The app works the same either way, and you can change your answer in Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.

Where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, Google's consent form appears before the tracking prompt, and you can choose again under privacy choices in the Info section of Settings.

faq.q: Life Tally Pro and restoring the purchase
a: Tap the Pro row in Settings to open the Life Tally Pro screen and buy it there. You pay once, and it is not a subscription. Records, Upcoming, reminders, backup and iCloud, and the lock all work without buying.
On a new device or after reinstalling, tap restore purchase at the bottom of the same screen. With the same Apple Account, you won't be charged again.
Export to Excel in Life Tally Pro turns all your records into a CSV file that opens in Excel and hands it to the iOS share sheet. You choose where the file goes in the share sheet.
Writing and viewing records work offline. iCloud sync, ads, buying Life Tally Pro and restoring the purchase, and filling in from a link need a connection.
Close the app completely, open it again, and check that you have the latest version from the App Store. If the problem continues, email us with the screen you were on and what you were doing.

privacy.title: Life Tally Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: The developer does not collect personal information. Records are stored on your device and, when you are signed in to iCloud, synced through your own iCloud. The banner ad comes from Google AdMob, which processes device information such as the advertising identifier. Apple handles payment for Life Tally Pro.
intro: kvndh ("the developer") handles the personal information of people who use the Life Tally app ("the app") under Korea's Personal Information Protection Act, as set out below.

sections.title: Purpose of processing
paragraphs: The app has no sign-up or login, and the developer does not collect personal information from users. The app uses the records you write to show totals per person, Your turn, upcoming occasions and reminders, and the developer has no server.

The app shows one banner ad at the bottom of the Home, People and Settings tabs. Google's ad service AdMob selects and displays that ad, and uses device information to show ads and measure how they perform.

sections.title: Information processed
paragraphs: The developer collects no personal information. The data the app uses is listed below and is kept in the app's storage on your device. When you are signed in to iCloud, people, envelope and upcoming records are also kept in your own iCloud. Records can include other people's names and birthdays and the amounts you exchanged, as you write them. The developer does not receive any of this data.
Information that AdMob may collect when showing ads is listed in section 9.
bullets: People (name, label, relationship, memo, birthday month and day, whether it is lunar or in a leap month, year of birth): used for records per person and birthday reminders
Envelopes (given or received, date, occasion, whose event, amount, method, gift item, attendance, meal, tags, memo, thank-you mark): used for records and totals
Upcoming (title, type, date, place, memo): used for the Upcoming list and reminders
Your own events (title, type, whose event, date, memo) and the envelopes received at them: used for the guestbook in Life Tally Pro
Automatic copies (a copy of your records made once a day, the latest 14): used to bring back earlier records

App settings (whether the lock and reminders are on, Hanja lettering on envelopes, the ledger currency, the order of the people list, a copy of the Life Tally Pro purchase check, the relationship and type lists you edited, markers for one-time data tidy-ups): used to run the app. Records such as people and envelopes are not kept here

sections.title: Processing and retention period
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal information. Data in the app's storage and the automatic copies are deleted when you delete the app, and only the latest 14 automatic copies are kept, with older ones removed. Records synced to iCloud remain in your own iCloud account. Backup files and CSV files you send through the share sheet stay where you put them, and you can delete them there.
Information collected by AdMob is kept according to Google's Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy).

sections.title: Disclosure to third parties
paragraphs: The developer does not provide users' personal information to third parties. However, the Google Mobile Ads SDK and Google User Messaging Platform SDK built into the app send the information in section 9 directly to Google, as follows.
bullets: Recipient: Google LLC (United States), AdMob
Purpose: checking ad consent, showing ads and measuring ad performance
Information: the device information and ad interaction records listed in section 9
When and how: sent over the internet when ad consent is checked and when an ad is loaded and shown
Retention: as set out in Google's Privacy Policy

sections.title: Outsourcing of processing
paragraphs: The developer does not outsource the processing of personal information. iCloud sync runs on Apple's iCloud (CloudKit), and synced data is governed by Apple's privacy policy. Apple processes payment for Life Tally Pro through the App Store. The developer does not receive your payment method, your Apple Account details or what is in your iCloud.

sections.title: Destruction of information
paragraphs: The developer holds no personal information, so there is nothing to destroy. Data in the app's storage and the automatic copies are removed when you delete the app. Records synced to iCloud are managed in your own Apple Account.

sections.title: Rights of users and legal guardians, and how to exercise them
paragraphs: Because the developer holds no personal information, there is nothing to access, correct, or delete. Records synced to iCloud are in your own Apple Account, and the developer cannot view or delete them. If you have questions, email us at the address below.

You can ask Google to give you access to, or delete, information collected by AdMob (policies.google.com/privacy). To refuse use of the advertising identifier, follow section 9. Payment information is held by Apple and is covered by Apple's privacy policy (apple.com/legal/privacy).

sections.title: Security measures
paragraphs: Records are kept in the app's storage on the device, and iCloud sync uses the private database (CloudKit) in your own iCloud account. The developer has no server. When the lock is on in Settings, the app asks for iOS device authentication (Face ID or the device passcode) when it opens, and face data is not passed to the app. The app asks for notification permission only when you turn on reminders in Settings, and reminders for occasions and birthdays are local notifications scheduled on the device. Fill in from a photo in Life Tally Pro receives only the one photo you choose in the iOS photo picker and reads its text on the device, and the app does not send the photo anywhere or store it. The app does not ask for access to your photo library. Fill in from a link opens the invitation or obituary page you paste in a hidden web view that keeps no cookies or browsing history, and reads its text. The server of that page receives the request as with any web visit, and the app does not send the text it reads anywhere else. Backup files and CSV files are made only when you tap, and are handed to the iOS share sheet.

sections.title: Automatic collection and how to refuse it
paragraphs: The app does not use cookies or analytics tools. It includes the Google Mobile Ads SDK (AdMob) and Google User Messaging Platform SDK for advertising, which may collect the information below when they check ad consent and load and show ads.

When the app gets ads ready, iOS shows the App Tracking Transparency (ATT) prompt asking whether to allow tracking. If you don't allow tracking, AdMob does not receive the advertising identifier (IDFA), and you can use the app the same way. You can change this in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking.

In regions where ad consent is required, such as the European Economic Area, Google's consent form appears before the tracking prompt. There, you can change your choices under privacy choices in the Info section of Settings.

After you buy Life Tally Pro, no ads appear. When the app opens, it checks the purchase, and with Life Tally Pro it does not check consent, show the tracking prompt or start the SDK. If you buy while the app is open, the banner disappears right away, but an SDK already started in that session stays until you close the app and is not started from the next launch.
bullets: Device identifiers, and the advertising identifier (IDFA) if you allow tracking
Approximate location estimated from your IP address
Ad interaction records such as impressions and taps

sections.title: Privacy officer
paragraphs: If you have questions about personal information, email us at the address below.

sections.title: Remedies for privacy concerns
paragraphs: If you need advice about a privacy concern or help settling a dispute, you can contact the Korean bodies listed below. If you live outside Korea, you can also contact the data protection authority in your country.
bullets: Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee: 1833-6972 in Korea (www.kopico.go.kr)
Personal Information Infringement Report Center: 118 in Korea (privacy.kisa.or.kr)
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: 1301 in Korea (www.spo.go.kr)
National Police Agency: 182 in Korea (ecrm.police.go.kr)
European Union and EEA: the data protection authority of your country (edpb.europa.eu)
United Kingdom: Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk)
United States: Federal Trade Commission (reportfraud.ftc.gov)
Other countries: the data protection or consumer protection authority where you live
